newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down amid finance results concern.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down amid finance results concern.

text.p: Investors unloaded key stocks after finding first quarter earnings results of finance firms released on Monday unimpressive focing the stock index to drop by the close on Monday, brokers said.

"The release of first quarter earnings of several finance companies dominated market sentiment today. Although some results matched earlier expectations, they still created negative feeling among investors," said Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia.
The composite SET index slipped 6.02 points to 694.21 on 3.1 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index slipped 0.61 point to 52.68.
Decliners led gainers 196 to 74 while 93 issues remained unchanged.
Brokers said most first quarter earnings of finance firms, released through the bourse today, did not disappoint investors' as the generally poorer results were expected.
Brokers said finance firms and banks, hit by slowing economic growth and increased provisioning requirements, had been expected to post less first quarter earnings.
They said stock trading was also muted ahead of the central bank's release of key monthly economic data on Thursday.

Most of the key sectors declined today. The banking sector topped the active list in terms of value, falling 0.37 percent, followed by the communication sector which gained 1.59 percent and the finance sector which fell 1.69 percent.
Siam Makro topped the active list, advancing three baht to 70. Bangkok Bank fell two to 185 and BEC World shed four to 236.
Support is seen by some brokers at 680 while resistance is pegged at 710 for Tuesday.
